authority.summary: Drupal core's default.settings.php documents the environment-specific nature of settings overrides, which is why this rule refuses to assert a production defect.

context_requirements.subject: deployment
context_requirements.why_it_matters: Verbose error display is normal in development and inappropriate in production. No environment evidence is observable from a repository, so this cannot be called a production defect.

finding.assertion: Exported configuration sets system.logging error_level to verbose.

conclusion.candidate: Errors including backtraces are exported as displayed. Whether that reaches production depends on environment overrides this analysis cannot see.
conclusion.not_observed: The exported configuration does not set verbose error display.
conclusion.unknown: The exported error level could not be established.

finding.evidence_explanation: system.logging:error_level was observed as 'verbose' in exported configuration.
limitations: No environment evidence is observable from a repository, so this is never a production claim.

remediation.guidance: Confirm which environments receive this exported value, and whether a production settings override changes it.

review.authority: reviewed against the pinned default.settings.php snapshot

scope.notes: The error_level setting exists in Drupal 8 and later.

summary: The exported system.logging configuration displays all errors including backtraces. Whether that is wrong depends on the environment, which this analysis cannot observe.
title: Verbose error display is exported without observable environment context
